themes_detail.label: Street vending enforcement surge
themes_detail.summary: Vendor Enforcement complaints exploded to 8 this week versus a baseline of 0.2 per week over the prior 8 weeks—a 3,900% spike (z-score: 17.9)—suggesting either a sudden enforcement crackdown or rapid increase in street vending complaints in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 8 Vendor Enforcement complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.2 weekly average over prior 8 weeks (z-score: 17.9)
3,100% increase represents most extreme statistical spike in entire complaint dataset
Coincides with Illegal Posting spike (5 complaints this week vs. 0.1 avg), suggesting coordinated city enforcement activity
reporting_angles: Interview street vendors and community members about sudden enforcement action—who is being targeted and why?
Obtain NYPD/DOC enforcement records to confirm whether a specific operation launched this week
Examine whether this affects informal economy and food access in low-income neighborhood

themes_detail.label: Graffiti and illegal posting escalation
themes_detail.summary: Graffiti complaints spiked to 6 this week from a baseline of 0.4 per week (1,500% increase, z-score: 5.67), while Illegal Posting jumped to 5 complaints from 0.1 per week (3,900% increase, z-score: 14.74)—suggesting a coordinated vandalism campaign or deterioration in city cleanup response in Central Harlem this week.
evidence: 6 Graffiti complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.4 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 5.67)
5 Illegal Posting complaints THIS WEEK vs. 0.1 weekly average over 8 weeks (z-score: 14.74)
Temporal clustering suggests single causal event rather than independent spikes
reporting_angles: Map where graffiti and illegal posting complaints are concentrated—is there a specific corridor or neighborhood block?
Interview Parks Department or Sanitation about cleanup timelines and whether they've mobilized additional resources
Document visual conditions with photos and canvass residents about what they've observed

themes_detail.label: Rodent infestation acceleration
themes_detail.summary: Rodent complaints jumped to 33 two weeks ago from a baseline of 15.8 per week (110% increase, z-score: 5.4)—a sustained signal suggesting active pest infestation problems across Central Harlem despite the baseline already being elevated.
evidence: 33 Rodent complaints 2 weeks ago vs. 15.8 weekly baseline (110% increase, z-score: 5.4)
Rodent issues are high-frequency chronic problem (part of top 10 complaint types by volume)
Spike timing aligns with warming season but magnitude exceeds seasonal norm
reporting_angles: Interview residents and building owners about specific locations with rodent problems—residential, commercial, or both?
Investigate whether complaint spike is driven by particular buildings or citywide in the district
Query Health Department about inspection results and violations issued in past 2 weeks

themes_detail.label: Illegal parking and vehicle abandonment surge
themes_detail.summary: Illegal Parking complaints jumped 83% last week (136 complaints vs. 74.2 weekly average, z-score: 5.06), while Abandoned Vehicle complaints surged 315% last week (14 vs. 3.4 average, z-score: 4.64)—suggesting either a parking crisis or a shift in enforcement priorities in Central Harlem.
evidence: 136 Illegal Parking complaints LAST WEEK vs. 74.2 weekly average (83% increase, z-score: 5.06)
14 Abandoned Vehicle complaints LAST WEEK vs. 3.4 weekly average (315% increase, z-score: 4.64)
Illegal Parking already in top 10 highest-volume complaint categories (1,133 complaints over 90 days)
reporting_angles: Determine whether spike reflects actual increase in parking violations or increased reporting/enforcement
Interview NYPD Traffic or Sanitation about abandoned vehicle removal operations last week
Assess whether new development activity (459 DOB permits filed in 90 days) is constraining available parking

themes_detail.label: Food establishment inspection spike
themes_detail.summary: Food Establishment complaints jumped to 9 two weeks ago from a baseline of 3.2 per week (177% increase, z-score: 4.43)—suggesting potential health code violations or sanitation concerns at restaurants and food vendors in Central Harlem two weeks ago.
evidence: 9 Food Establishment complaints 2 WEEKS AGO vs. 3.2 weekly average (177% increase, z-score: 4.43)
Complaint spike temporal coincides with other public health concerns (Unsanitary Condition is top complaint type: 1,316 over 90 days)
Food Establishment spikes are less frequent than parking/heat/noise, making anomaly more notable
reporting_angles: Obtain Health Department inspection records for past 2-3 weeks—which establishments received violations?
Interview Health Department about what types of violations were cited
Canvass affected restaurants for context about why violations occurred
